previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with chest pain and a brief syncopal episode following a polysubstance binge involving cocaine, heroin, and alcohol. He has a significant cardiac history including prior stents and reduced ejection fraction. Evaluation showed no acute heart attack, with normal troponins and EKG changes consistent with prior infarcts. The chest pain and syncope were attributed to demand ischemia likely triggered by cocaine use. Psychiatry evaluated and cleared him, and he was deemed medically stable for discharge. He was counseled on the dangers of substance use, particularly cocaine with his heart condition, and advised to avoid combining metoprolol with cocaine. He was discharged home with instructions to follow up with his PCP and counselor, though he left without taking discharge paperwork due to attending his nephew’s wake.

Brief Hospital Course:
PRIMARY REASON FOR ADMISSION 
___ yo male with significant CAD history s/p 4 stents who 
presents with chest pain in the setting of heroine/alcohol 
withdrawal.   
.
ACTIVE ISSUES
.
# Chest pain- Patient noted to have central non-radiating chest 
pain while in ED observation. Patient has a long complex 
coronary artery disease history with several stents in the past. 
His pain was not felt to represent acute coronary syndrome. EKG 
showed Q waves in V1-V4 consistent with a previous anterior MI 
that was unchanged from previous. Patient was ruled out for an 
MI with troponins that were negative x 3. The patients pain was 
felt to be atypical in nature and most likely related to 
withdrawal from alcohol and heroine. However it was felt that 
there may be a component of anginal pain in the setting of 
hypertension.  Therefore he was started on Imdur 30 mg daily. 
The patient ultimately decided to leave against medical advice 
and was advised to make an appointment to ___ with his 
primary care physician. 
.
# Withdrawal- Patient was noted to be intoxicated on admission 
with an EtOH level of 355. Per the patient report he had been on 
a 5 day binge of several quarts of vodka, heroine and cocaine 
previous to being brought to the hospital by EMS.  His serum 
toxic screen was positive for ethanol as above and urine 
toxicology screen was notably positive for opioids but negative 
for cocaine.  The patient was started on a CIWA scale with 10 mg 
Valium every 2 hours.  He was noted to have significant 
withdrawal symptoms most notably tremors and diarrhea but denied 
any hallucinations or suicidal or homicidal ideation. The 
patient was also hypertensive with SBP in the 150s and 
tachycardic with HR to 106. Symptoms persisted however the 
patient ultimately decided to leave against medical advice.  
Patient was informed of and expressed understanding of the risks 
of leaving while in active withdrawal including seizure, cardiac 
disease, and death. He was seen by social work who provided him 
with information regarding rehab facilities two of which may 
have beds available tomorrow.  The patient was encouraged to 
call these facilities and reports he will make theses calls 
tomorrow. 
.
# Hypertension- Patient noted to have elevated blood pressure on 
admission.  Per the patients report he had not been taking his 
home anti-hypertensives for the past several days.  The patient 
was restarted on his home lisinopril. His metoprolol was held 
due to concern for recent cocaine use. He should ___ with 
his PCP regarding restarting this medication. He additionally 
was started on Imdur 30 mg daily. 
.
STABLE ISSUES
.
# Coronary Artery Disease- As above the patient had not been 
compliant with his home regimen.  He was restarted on his home 
ASA 325 mg, Plavix 75 mg, pravastatin 40 mg and lisinopril 10 
mg.  As above his home metoprolol was held during this admission 
and at the time of discharge. 
.
# Hyperlipidemia- patient was continued on his home pravastatin. 

.
# Anxiety and Depression- Patient was continued on his 
citalopram.  His clonazepam was held while he was getting 
Valium.  He was continued on his home clonazepam at the time of 
discharge. As above the patient was denying any homicidal or 
suicidal ideation currently or in the past.  
.

- Patient should call his PCP to make an appointment on ___ 
- Patient remained full code throughout this hospitalization
